production.note: US model years. First: Toyota's newsroom album '2013 – 2014 Scion FR-S [First (1st) Generation]'. Last: Scion's brochure for 'MODEL YEAR 2016' (scion-us-2016-fr-s-brochure); for 2017 'the Scion FR-S adopts the Toyota 86 identity used in other global markets, as Scion and its models transition back to the Toyota brand' (toyota-us-2017-86-release). The 2017 to 2020 car is the separate Toyota 86 record.

body.note: Inferred: Scion describes a two-door, rear-wheel-drive boxer-engined sports car; sold only as a coupe.

aspiration.note: Inferred: the brochure describes a 2.0-liter boxer four with no turbocharger or supercharger.

fuel.note: Inferred from the brochure's description of a conventional piston engine.

transmission.note: '6-SPEED MANUAL OR 6-SPEED AUTOMATIC WITH PADDLE SHIFTERS AND DYNAMIC REV MANAGEMENT™'

powerHp.note: 2014 model year. Quote: "HORSEPOWER(1). . . 200 HP @ 7,000 RPM". No opened page gives the FR-S any other rating; the 205 hp manual rating arrived with the renamed 2017 Toyota 86, which got 'a five-horsepower increase to 205 hp' (toyota-us-2017-86-release).

weightLb.note: 2014 model year, 6-speed manual. Quote: "CURB WEIGHT . . . 2,758 LBS. MT / 2,806 LBS. AT". No Scion or Toyota weight for the 2013 launch year was found (the 2013 brochure is not on Auto-Brochures), so the reference year is 2014, the earliest year with a manufacturer figure; the power rating is the same in both years.
